explanation: The sources put the two together and put the resentment on the record: the government was against the British pressure — the seizure of Brazilian ships by British warships — and legislated under it anyway, five years after the Act and this time with enforcement behind the text. The law of 1831 had been a dead letter for nineteen years; what changed between 1831 and 1850 was not Brazilian opinion about slavery, which did not change until much later, but the cost of continuing.
